coverage_questions: The paper does not provide Supplementary Table S3, Supplementary Fig. S4, or task-specific prompt templates; exact lexical templates, delimiters, answer teacher-forcing receipt, and task-specific field values remain unspecified.
The 23 downstream tasks are described collectively rather than as separate input specifications, so their shared sequence-only fine-tuning and evaluation path is grouped.

The paper reports three OmniNA parameter scales, while the atlas names generic OmniNA and OmniNA-1.7B; generic trajectories cover the shared family architecture and explicit OmniNA-1.7B trajectories cover the named 1.7B variant.
The paper does not specify the exact input prompt used for generation experiments beyond sequence-only deployment and generation controls.
The feature-representation section does not specify the exact tokenizer-to-sequence aggregation implementation, transformer-layer extraction interface, or complete special-token and mask handling.
The saturation-mutation equations are not decoded; the paired log-likelihood-difference scoring boundary is retained as unresolved.

operation_proposals.why_no_existing_operation: The catalog contains probabilistic sampling but no beam-search or deterministic sequence-search primitive. The paper explicitly specifies beam search for generation.
The catalog has no operation for evaluating autoregressive target log-likelihoods and computing their paired difference between two aligned sequences.
The catalog has no reduction or mean-pooling operation for averaging sub-token embedding vectors into one vocabulary- or sequence-level representation.

evidence.quote: We designed prompts to organize the sequence data with textual annotations as feature-ordered input for model pre-training.
The pretraining objective was nexttoken prediction, where the model learned to predict the subsequent nucleotide or annotation token given the preceding context.
